statement: FEV1 declines progressively with age in healthy adults (~25-30 mL/yr after the mid-20s plateau), with smoking steepening the slope and cessation resetting the rate of decline toward that of a never-smoker.
effect_size: ~25-30 mL/yr FEV1 decline in healthy never-smokers; steeper in smokers; cessation normalizes decline rate (not recovers lost function)
population: Working men, original Fletcher-Peto cohort and successors

provenance.primary: Fletcher C, Peto R - 'The natural history of chronic airflow obstruction', BMJ 1977
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-17 organ-systems atlas; PubMed PMID lookup

confidence_notes: Foundational COPD/lung-aging framework. Quitting does not reverse lost FEV1 but changes the future slope - the central honest message for respiratory longevity.

statement: COPD can arise either from accelerated FEV1 decline from a normal peak OR from never reaching a normal peak in early adulthood; lung aging is partly set in childhood.
effect_size: ~half of COPD cases in the cohort arose from low peak lung function rather than accelerated decline
population: Three large longitudinal cohorts (Framingham Offspring, CCHS, COPDGene)

provenance.primary: Lange P, Celli B, et al. - 'Lung-Function Trajectories Leading to Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease', NEJM 2015

confidence_notes: Reframes lung aging as partly developmental; refines the single-slope Fletcher-Peto model.

statement: Exercise-based pulmonary rehabilitation improves exercise capacity and quality of life in COPD.
effect_size: Clinically meaningful improvements in exercise capacity and health-related quality of life vs usual care

provenance.primary: McCarthy B, et al. - 'Pulmonary rehabilitation for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2015

confidence_notes: Improves function/symptoms; does not regenerate lung tissue. Honest: a function lever, not a structural cure.

statement: High-resistance inspiratory muscle strength training (~5 min/day) lowers systolic blood pressure and improves endothelial function in midlife/older adults.
effect_size: ~9 mmHg reduction in systolic BP; improved endothelial function vs sham
population: Midlife and older adults with above-normal BP

provenance.primary: Craighead DH, et al. - 'Time-Efficient Inspiratory Muscle Strength Training Lowers Blood Pressure and Improves Endothelial Function', J Am Heart Assoc 2021

confidence_notes: The strongest 'breathing device' evidence - but the benefit is CARDIOVASCULAR (BP), not increased lung capacity. Do not conflate with 'growing your lungs'.

statement: Inspiratory muscle training increases inspiratory muscle strength but adds little to patient-important outcomes over pulmonary rehabilitation alone in COPD.
effect_size: Improved inspiratory muscle strength; limited incremental benefit over rehab alone

provenance.primary: Ammous O, et al. - 'Inspiratory muscle training, with or without concomitant pulmonary rehabilitation, for COPD', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2023

confidence_notes: Tempers IMT hype for respiratory disease specifically.

statement: Higher cardiorespiratory fitness is associated with lower all-cause mortality with no observed upper limit of benefit; the lowest-fitness quintile carries risk comparable to or exceeding smoking, diabetes, or end-stage renal disease.
effect_size: Monotonic mortality reduction with fitness; lowest vs elite fitness HR comparable to major chronic diseases

provenance.primary: Mandsager K, et al. - 'Association of Cardiorespiratory Fitness With Long-term Mortality Among Adults Undergoing Exercise Treadmill Testing', JAMA Network Open 2018

confidence_notes: VO2max is a spectacular PREDICTOR; the LEVER is the aerobic training that raises it (predictor != lever). Cross-ref Domain E.

statement: Each 1-MET increase in cardiorespiratory fitness is associated with ~13% lower all-cause and ~15% lower cardiovascular mortality.
effect_size: ~13% lower all-cause and ~15% lower CHD/CVD mortality per 1-MET higher fitness

provenance.primary: Kodama S, et al. - 'Cardiorespiratory Fitness as a Quantitative Predictor of All-Cause Mortality and Cardiovascular Events', JAMA 2009

confidence_notes: Quantifies the fitness-mortality gradient; observational, healthy-user effects not fully excluded.

statement: Estimated GFR declines roughly 0.8-1.0 mL/min/1.73m2 per year after age ~40 due to nephron dropout, and the kidney is clinically silent until advanced disease.
effect_size: ~0.8-1.0 mL/min/1.73m2/yr eGFR decline after 40 ('~1%/yr')

provenance.primary: Romagnani P, et al. - 'Chronic kidney disease', Nature Reviews Disease Primers 2017

confidence_notes: Raises the interpretive question of how much late-life CKD-stage-3 is disease vs expected aging. Silent system - prevention played on proxy numbers, not symptoms.

statement: Declining eGFR independently predicts incident frailty and mortality in older adults.
effect_size: eGFR decline associated with higher incident frailty and mortality independent of baseline

provenance.primary: Guerville F, et al. - 'Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate Decline and Incident Frailty in Older Adults', Clin J Am Soc Nephrol 2019

confidence_notes: Predictor, not necessarily a modifiable lever in the elderly (predictor != lever).

statement: Hypertension and diabetes are the two dominant modifiable drivers of kidney function loss; blood pressure and glucose control slow CKD progression.
effect_size: BP control, glucose control, RAAS blockade and SGLT2 inhibition slow eGFR decline in CKD

provenance.primary: Kalantar-Zadeh K, et al. - 'Chronic kidney disease', Lancet 2021

confidence_notes: The kidney has almost no direct lever - you protect it by protecting the vasculature/metabolism.

statement: Chronic under-hydration, reflected in higher-normal serum sodium, is associated with accelerated biological aging, more chronic disease, and earlier mortality.
effect_size: Higher-normal serum sodium associated with higher biological age, chronic disease risk and mortality

provenance.primary: Dmitrieva NI, et al. - 'Middle-age high normal serum sodium as a risk factor for accelerated biological aging, chronic diseases, and premature mortality', EBioMedicine 2023

confidence_notes: Honest reading: 'avoid chronic under-hydration', NOT 'force liters'. Association only; no RCT shows pushing extra fluid in adequately-hydrated people extends life (predictor != lever).

statement: High dietary protein intake does not cause kidney disease in people with healthy kidneys; transient hyperfiltration is a normal adaptation, and protein needs in older adults may exceed the RDA.
effect_size: No evidence of renal harm from high protein in normal-kidney adults; higher intakes support muscle preservation

provenance.primary: Phillips SM, et al. - 'Protein requirements beyond the RDA: implications for optimizing health', Appl Physiol Nutr Metab 2016

confidence_notes: Debunks the protein-harms-kidneys myth for HEALTHY kidneys. Different conversation in established CKD. Don't let the myth talk an aging adult out of needed protein.

statement: In adults with reduced kidney function, higher animal (but not plant) protein intake is associated with faster eGFR decline.
effect_size: Higher animal protein associated with faster eGFR decline; plant protein neutral-to-protective
population: Adults with and without CKD, observational cohort

provenance.primary: Bernier-Jean A, et al. - 'Dietary plant and animal protein intake and decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate', Nephrol Dial Transplant 2021

confidence_notes: Context nuance: applies to established/reduced kidney function and points to protein SOURCE. Not a contradiction of the healthy-kidney finding - a context split (cohort != RCT).

statement: NSAIDs reduce renal blood flow and can cause acute kidney injury (especially with dehydration, older age, or ACE-inhibitor/diuretic co-use), and chronic heavy use is associated with CKD progression.
effect_size: Increased AKI risk (esp. 'triple whammy'); association with CKD progression with chronic heavy use

provenance.primary: Baker M, Perazella MA - 'NSAIDs in CKD: Are They Safe?', Am J Kidney Dis 2020

confidence_notes: A free, modifiable lever most people ignore: don't make NSAIDs a daily default, hydrate when using, caution if older/on BP meds.

statement: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD, formerly NAFLD) now affects ~30%+ of adults globally and is rising; fibrosis stage is the key prognostic axis.
effect_size: Global prevalence ~30-38% of adults and increasing

provenance.primary: Younossi ZM, et al. - 'The Global Epidemiology of Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease and Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis', Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol 2024

confidence_notes: The hepatic face of insulin resistance; fibrosis (not steatosis) predicts mortality. Tightly linked to obesity/T2D/CVD.

statement: NAFLD was renamed MASLD (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease) by multisociety consensus to center the metabolic etiology.
effect_size: Nomenclature change adopted by major hepatology societies (Delphi consensus)

provenance.primary: Rinella ME, et al. - 'A multisociety Delphi consensus statement on new fatty liver disease nomenclature', J Hepatol 2023

confidence_notes: Definitional/framing claim; reflects the metabolic-liver reframe.

statement: Weight loss reverses liver histology in NASH/MASH in a dose-response manner: >=7% loss resolves steatohepatitis in most patients and >=10% produces fibrosis regression in a majority.
effect_size: >=7% weight loss resolved NASH in ~64-90%; >=10% regressed fibrosis in a majority (paired biopsies)
population: 261 patients with biopsy-proven NASH, 52-week lifestyle program

provenance.primary: Vilar-Gomez E, et al. - 'Weight Loss Through Lifestyle Modification Significantly Reduces Features of Nonalcoholic Steatohepatitis', Gastroenterology 2015

confidence_notes: Prospective paired-histology dose-response - about as strong as the field gets. The one intervention that reverses liver histology. The liver has no special lever; it heals when metabolism does.

statement: Commercial 'liver detox' teas, juices, and cleanse protocols have no credible evidence of enhancing hepatic detoxification or removing toxins, and some such products are themselves hepatotoxic.
effect_size: No quality clinical evidence for detox/cleanse efficacy; documented cases of supplement-induced liver injury

provenance.primary: Klein AV, Kiat H - 'Detox diets for toxin elimination and weight management: a critical review of the evidence', J Hum Nutr Diet 2015 (and herbal/supplement DILI literature)
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-17 organ-systems atlas; domain knowledge + DILI literature

confidence_notes: Flat debunk. The liver detoxifies itself; the only evidence-based help is LESS work (less alcohol, fewer excess calories, fewer needless supplements, weight loss).

statement: Gastrointestinal motility slows with age (reduced enteric neuron density, weaker peristalsis, impaired esophageal clearance), but much age-attributed constipation is secondary to medications, immobility, low fiber/fluid and comorbidity.
effect_size: Slowed transit and higher constipation prevalence with age; large secondary/modifiable component

provenance.primary: Gidwaney NG, et al. - 'Gastrointestinal Dysmotility in the Elderly', J Clin Gastroenterol 2016

confidence_notes: More modifiable than 'old gut' fatalism implies - fiber, fluid, movement, medication review.

statement: Lifestyle measures (especially weight loss, plus head-of-bed elevation, avoiding late meals, and trigger-food identification) are first-line for GERD and reduce reliance on chronic acid suppression.
effect_size: Weight loss is the best-evidenced lifestyle lever; positional and dietary measures add benefit

provenance.primary: Katz PO, et al. - 'ACG Clinical Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease', Am J Gastroenterol 2022

confidence_notes: PPIs effective when indicated; chronic reflux is often a weight-and-mechanics problem. Goal: lowest effective drug dose, not reflexive indefinite suppression.

statement: Higher dietary fiber intake is associated with 15-30% lower all-cause and cardiovascular mortality, with a dose-response and lower incidence of CHD, stroke, type 2 diabetes and colorectal cancer.
effect_size: ~15-30% lower all-cause and CVD mortality (highest vs lowest fiber); dose-response
population: WHO-commissioned series: 185 prospective studies + 58 RCTs (intermediate endpoints)

provenance.primary: Reynolds A, et al. - 'Carbohydrate quality and human health: a series of systematic reviews and meta-analyses', Lancet 2019

confidence_notes: Mortality endpoints are cohort-derived ('strongly associated'), but mechanism + intermediate-endpoint RCTs + consistent cohorts make it about as solid as nutritional epidemiology gets. Cross-ref C2/D.

statement: Anemia prevalence climbs steeply after 65 and independently predicts hospitalization, disability and mortality; it usually signals an underlying disease rather than 'old blood'.
effect_size: Anemia independently associated with higher hospitalization and mortality in older adults

provenance.primary: Culleton BF, et al. - 'Impact of anemia on hospitalization and mortality in older adults', Blood 2006

confidence_notes: Predictor/flag - the lever is finding and treating the CAUSE (iron, B12, CKD, occult bleed), not the number (predictor != lever).

statement: Hereditary (HFE) hemochromatosis causes iron overload damaging liver, heart, pancreas and joints; therapeutic phlebotomy (regular bloodletting/donation) depletes iron stores and normalizes life expectancy if started before organ damage.
effect_size: Phlebotomy to target ferritin prevents/limits organ damage; near-normal life expectancy if pre-cirrhotic

provenance.primary: Kowdley KV, et al. - 'ACG Clinical Guideline: Hereditary Hemochromatosis', Am J Gastroenterol 2019

confidence_notes: The one genetic disease where a blood-donation needle is the treatment ('donation angle'). Guideline/long-standing standard of care.

statement: The 'iron hypothesis' that routine blood donation reduces cardiovascular risk by lowering body iron is a plausible mechanism with confounded and inconsistent human evidence (healthy-donor effect).
effect_size: Some donor cohorts show lower CVD/IMT, but confounded by healthy-donor selection; not consistently replicated

provenance.primary: Sullivan JL - 'Blood donation may be good for the donor. Iron, heart disease, and donor recruitment', Vox Sang 1991

confidence_notes: Donate to help others and as therapy if you have iron overload - NOT as a proven longevity hack for the general population.

statement: Vitamin B12 deficiency is common and under-diagnosed in older adults (atrophic gastritis, reduced acid, metformin use) and causes anemia plus a potentially irreversible neurologic/cognitive picture.
effect_size: Elevated deficiency prevalence with age and metformin use; reversible if caught early, neuro damage can be permanent if not

provenance.primary: Green R, et al. - 'Vitamin B12 deficiency', Vitamins and Hormones 2022

confidence_notes: Cheap, high-value test in older/symptomatic adults; repletion easy and effective. Metformin lowers B12 (Bell, Diabetes Obes Metab 2022, 10.1111/dom.14734).

statement: Venous thromboembolism incidence rises sharply (roughly exponentially) with age due to slower venous flow, more procoagulant factors, immobility and accumulating provoking events.
effect_size: Roughly exponential rise in VTE incidence with age

provenance.primary: Lind MM, et al. - 'Incidence and risk factors of venous thromboembolism in men and women', Thromb Res 2022

confidence_notes: Non-pharmacologic levers: mobility, hydration, awareness of provoking situations. Anticoagulation is a clinical decision (owned by section 07).

statement: Erectile dysfunction is an independent early-warning marker of systemic vascular disease, often preceding coronary events by years because penile arteries are small and show endothelial dysfunction first.
effect_size: ED independently associated with increased incident cardiovascular disease (umbrella review)
population: Men, pooled cohorts and umbrella review

provenance.primary: Mostafaei H, et al. - 'Association of erectile dysfunction and cardiovascular disease: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses', BJU Int 2021

confidence_notes: Purest predictor != lever case: ED predicts heart disease; the lever is CV work-up + risk-factor control, NOT silencing the symptom with a PDE5 inhibitor. A useful, free signal.

statement: The benefit/risk of menopausal hormone therapy depends on timing relative to menopause onset (the 'timing hypothesis'); early initiation has a more favorable cardiovascular/bone profile.
effect_size: More favorable risk/benefit when started near menopause onset vs later; still-evolving evidence
population: Recently menopausal women (KEEPS and related trials)

provenance.primary: Miller VM, et al. - 'The Kronos Early Estrogen Prevention Study (KEEPS): what have we learned?', Menopause 2019

confidence_notes: Brief cross-ref to N-womens-longevity.md / Domain 13 for full treatment. Hormones are powerful levers with real trade-offs, not free anti-aging.

statement: Complete decongestive therapy (compression, exercise, skin care, and manual lymphatic drainage) reduces limb volume in diagnosed lymphedema, but compression and exercise do most of the work and the MLD-massage component adds modest, sometimes non-significant value.
effect_size: CDT reduces limb volume; MLD adds little over compression alone in pooled RCTs

provenance.primary: Thompson B, et al. - 'Manual lymphatic drainage treatment for lymphedema: a systematic review of the literature', J Cancer Surviv 2021

confidence_notes: Two-tier honesty: CDT is standard care for real lymphedema, but the massage component is the weakest part. Basis for the wellness-MLD debunk.

statement: Claims that 'lymphatic drainage massage' detoxifies, boosts immunity, removes toxins, or reduces cellulite in healthy people are not supported by evidence; a healthy lymphatic system drains without manual help.
effect_size: No credible evidence for 'detox/immunity/cellulite' lymphatic-massage claims in healthy individuals

provenance.primary: Extrapolated from Thompson B, et al. J Cancer Surviv 2021 (MLD adds little even in disease) + absence of supporting evidence in healthy people

confidence_notes: Debunk. Pleasant/relaxing is a fine reason to enjoy a massage; it is not a health intervention. The honest lymphatic lever is movement - muscle contraction is the lymphatic pump.

statement: Smoking cessation is the single most effective respiratory-longevity intervention and resets the FEV1 decline rate toward that of a never-smoker at any age of quitting.
effect_size: Cessation normalizes decline rate; earlier quitting yields larger life-expectancy gains (cross-ref section 09 tobacco magnitude)

provenance.primary: Fletcher C, Peto R - 'The natural history of chronic airflow obstruction', BMJ 1977 (decline framework); cessation magnitude in section 09 tobacco literature

confidence_notes: Something beats nothing even in older quitters. Cross-ref 09-exposures-environment.md for the ~10-years-of-life tobacco magnitude.
